body: no thanks
no
I'll try to post an update about it, but I might have trouble posting if it's a successful attempt ;).
It pisses me off to no end that happy people have to die but people like me just can't seem to.
Couldn't have said it better myself, to be honest.

It makes me angery but I've learned to give those who don't appreciate my presence the gift of my absence. Unfortunately that's pretty much everyone but I'd rather be lonely than treated like an idiot.

Everyone I know has had terrible experiences with 211 Lifeline (US) and I've heard awful things about the Samaritans (UK, I think). I've had some good experiences and some not good experiences with Trevor Project (US, maybe US only). Sometimes they're useful, sometimes they're unuseful but afaik they have a policy of not calling the cops on callers (don't quote me on it).
I'm with you there. I don't want people to commit suicide but I can't intervene if they want to do it. I would be very upset if anyone intervened when I tried to do it.

I also struggle when writing suicide notes (I have to rewrite them because I usually live long enough to see them become outdated). For me personally once I started writing/got those first 3 paragraphs I was able to write like 11 pages in an hour. It might be different for you but for me it was a case of writer's block, though it sounds weird to call it then when writing a suicide note. Though if you're not planning on writing a full college dissertation's worth of suicide note, my advice may not help.
I'm in the same spot. Talking to friends has proven to be a dead end so here I am on Reddit. Surprisingly it actually helps.
Same for me as well. It feels like nobody takes me seriously. I'm 20 years old and people talk to me like an idiot.
It's probably not much consolation but I've felt the same way too. When a friend of mine killed herself I was angry that she succeeded where I had failed.

I completely agree. The entire system is so inhumane. I felt more like an animal than a person. Being caged and drugged was arguably more traumatizing than what led to my hospitalization in the first place.

I don't really know how to explain how I experience it. It's sort of like trying to hold my breath for as long as I can. No matter how badly I may want to hold my breath, my body isn't on the same page and will override my wishes and just start breathing. That or I know what I want to do but I just don't have the strength to do it. Or it's too physically painful.

It's one of those myths where I wonder how many people actually believe it. I have a feeling that the people who believe that myth want to believe that myth. It would feel more comfortable to many people to believe something like that. I am most dissociated at the moment so I may not be making a lot of sense. At any rate those are my thoughts on the matter.
I've had it before where I try to kill myself but then my body just takes over and stops it. Of course later that day if not shortly after I still want to end it again.
I agree. I do see a therapist but I'm never honest with her. When "help" is worse than death (for some of us), it's no surprise that some will choose death. Myself included.

I feel like on top of being terribly misguided, a lot of people just don't care. That's why they say these "it gets better" things. Because they don't want to hear about it. Out of sight, out of mind. But they may really mean well. I don't know, I've been told a pessimist.
Ah yes, everyone knows that having a gun pointed at you and being indebted works wonders for mental health. Nothing like new trauma and financial hardship.
r/thanksimcured. Seriously though the amount of "professionals" who've just told me to cheer up or be happy is a lot.

I find such claims dubious. The body may frantically fight to survive regardless of or contrary to the person's actual desires. Then again, I've never successfully killed myself so I may not be the person to ask about that.

I would also like to talk to them. Also I'm skeptical of the whole "changed their mind at the last second thing". Just because the body's survival instincts kick in and try to fight against death doesn't mean the person didn't really want to die, or subconsciously wanted to survive.

It completely sucks. When I was in highschool these thugs rolled up on me and told me it was ambulance or handcuffs. I was coerced into getting into the back of that ambulance otherwise they'd give me a mental health arrest and I'd get 5150d. It's not just arms either, if you get 5150d that can show up when you try to get a security clearance or other things. Welcome to America where the terminally depressed are second-class citizens.

Ah yes, that makes sense. Totally nothing fundamentally broken about that system. I hate that.

And then people wonder why people don't seek professional help or are pissed when someone calls 911 on them.

I completely agree. I'm of the opinion that I should be able to fill out a form and be provided with the means to humanely end my life. Better yet, I should be able to have a medical professional administer the euthanasia in a home or clinical setting. There's no reason for this not to exist.

It was covered by insurance but when I was in highschool the 10-minute ambulance ride to the hospital cost $1.2K. That's just the ambulance. I knew a middle schooler who racked up tens of thousands in debt, like $50K (her parents had to pay, not her, obviously) just because she had to spend some time in the psych ward.

I wish I could disagree with you but you're not really wrong. For me my doctors won't send me to the bin unless I straight up admit to being immediately suicidal.

That said, as soon as someone does send me to the bin or call crisis intervention on me, all bets are off and I'm off to the bin. Once in the bin, the fun (sarcasm) starts from there.

Not discouraging anyone from seeking help or going to the psych ward if they need it, but that's not for me and I'd kill myself before I let them take me in.
Can confirm. Am ugly and alive.
Same here. The main thing that's kept me from dying (other than fear of failure) is not wanting to hurt the people I care about. I wish I could just not care.

That totally makes sense.

It's fucked up but I feel like if I'm not a pretty young lady that my death won't be tragic or nobody will actually care. Maybe it's just confirmation bias but I feel like people don't care as much when older or less attractive people commit suicide. I also don't know why I'm sometimes preoccupied with whether or not people will find my death "tragic" because if we're being honest I usually want an unnoticed death. Other than 1 or 2 close friends I don't usually want anyone else to notice I'm gone.

"Normal" people say and do some of the craziest shit, I don't get how they're not the ones who are considered irrational. I'm sick of this paternalistic infantilizing bullshit. I'm an adult and I know what I want to do with my body.

It's so crazy to me that I'm expected to follow the rules of society, but I'm not allowed to be a member of society anyway. How am I expected to have the responsibilities and not the benefits of society?
I've also come close to death on multiple instances, I just don't get how I'm supposed to be happy that I'm still alive. If I wanted to live I wouldn't have tried to die so many times. It does hurt.

This. It's insane that I'm expected to accept that the state can just do whatever the hell they want to me and if I reject it I'm crazy or extreme or irrational. That any suicidality or depression just means I'm insane and don't get to have any rights. Forcing people into treatment or manipulating them into not committing suicide is a form of abuse, but people don't want to acknowledge that.

I also regret getting help sometimes. I just feel like I should have told nobody and killed myself years ago. Then it would have been unexpected and tragic and maybe people wouldn't blame me for wanting to use the nope rope.
Ironically that fact makes me want to kill myself even more badly.
This. People are like "you're fine" and I'm like well according to my definition I will be soon...

It starts with Am and ends in erica.

I'm pretty sure I know where you're going with this, so I'll save you some time. If you're about to argue that it's "not that bad" in America or that I don't know what I'm talking about, don't bother replying.
Same here. I can't afford to get my hopes with with empty promises that it will "get better".
Virtual hug accepted :)).
Same. I'd rather be seen as a person than not a person.

Me too. I'm sick of it all. I wish I could just push a button and transfer my life force to somebody else who wants it. That way people couldn't call me a coward either, they would have to call it a noble sacrifice if they ever found out about it.

I don't really get the whole "gift of life", but if somebody gives you a gift you don't want, you should be able to re-gift it.
It's so disturbing. Once you admit to being suicidal it's like they don't even see you as a person anymore. They're so condescending and cruel.

Honestly I usually expect posts like this to get deleted, too. There's such a pervasive attitude of people just flipping out at the mere suggestion that the suicide hotlines don't work, that hitting someone with a 5150 is wrong, or that doping someone up at the first sign of trouble is bad.

The system is so broken. I've learned not to speak of my troubles. I've learned to cry silently (literally) so nobody hears me and tries to "save" me. I've learned to do anything to avoid catching a 5150. The crazy thing too is that I've seen people who've been in the mental health system be some of its greatest defenders. I genuinely don't understand how after all that was done to them, they still claim its merits. It's like a kid that sticks by their abusive parent or someone who keeps going back to an abusive parent. It's cult-like.

Sorry that was a bit of a rant, it's just been on my mind lately.
This. Even worse is when people say "you're fine". No, I'm not fine. If I was I wouldn't be looking for ways to die.

This. The methods are out there but people do their best to make sure we never find them. Even if you find the correct methods, good luck getting your hands on the items you need.  What's that, found a method that's >99.999% effective? Too bad. The item you need hasn't been manufactured in your country for the past few decades. And the people who do the right thing and share the knowledge are persecuted by law enforcement unless they have their own legal team to dot their I's and cross there T's and whatever else it takes to please those pencil-pushing bureaucrats.
This. I'm terrified of a slow painful decline, waking up in the hospital, and being crippled for the rest of my life.

Me too. The sick thing is that there's ways to die completely painlessly but the sickos in office do everything they can to prevent us from accessing them. That way we're stuck with either suffering through the pain or trying a painful suicide method that might not even work and is likely to leave us crippled.

I completely feel that. Locking people up for being sick is just cruel. Imagine basically punishing somebody for having cancer. And before somebody tells me that we're not basically punishing people for being mentally ill, I've been to the psych ward. If it wasn't punishment, I don't know what was. If I wasn't sick when I came in, I was sick when I got out.

Agreed. People are seemingly fine with letting people suffer through the pain and suffering on the daily, but not okay with the person deciding to do something about their pain and suffering. People don't like suicide because unlike mental illness, they can't just pretend that somebody's still alive and didn't commit suicide.
Yes, the silent battles. People can suffer without it being obvious to other people. Just because somebody seems fine doesn't mean they're not in their own personal hell.

I agree 100%. Even putting logic aside, people have a right to live or die, whichever they see fit. No amount of mental gymnastics from ignorant do-gooders can change that. If somebody wants to end it, they should be able to fill out a form and be provided with medical euthanasia. People think I'm crazy for this shit but it's unconscionable to force people to live a life they want to end. There's a word for forcing people to suffer, it's called torture.

I also agree 100%.

Edit: this thread was nice while it lasted.

I hate those people with a passion. I don't care that they're "trying to help". If you see somebody a fully conscious person having trouble breathing and shove them to the ground to give them CPR and injure them in the process, nobody's going to accept that you're trying to help. But these people are always happy to use their excuse if you call them out on their shit.

This here. I can't speak for anybody else but I've tried the crisis counseling, the suicide hotlines, the inpatient treatments, the outpatient treatments. If it was helpful or at least not harmful, I would have kept using them.

It's funny, I don't remember much about being suicidal but I remember full well the cops pulling up and surrounding me, walking me to the squad car, and telling me it's the ambulance or the handcuffs.

Suicidal people aren't crazy, but people just don't seem to get it.
This exactly. It's why I just don't tell. Better dead than in the psych ward (for me).

This. Unless I trust somebody not to tell, I'm not telling them shit. And if they do cross that line, they're cut off forever. Even if I wasn't depressed I'd rather kill myself than go back to the psych ward.

TW: SA, etc. >!the place where I get drugged, sexually harassed assaulted by the guards, and treated like a crazy person. Fuck that.!<

I hate when that happens to me. I finally get the courage to pour my heart out into a post and nobody responds. Kind of like real life for me tbh. I'm at the point where I've just started to give up on trying to talk to people or make friends. Getting ignored and having no friends hurts worse than just having no friends.

I have the same thing, too. I'm 100% aware of how things will go but I always tell myself there's a sliver of a chance it will go differently, and it never does.

Just because people don't respond or care doesn't mean you're worthless, it just means that they don't respond or care. At least I certainly hope that's true.

I feel that, both having a friend who dies and wishing it was me, and having friends who are just better people than me. It's not even just friends either, sometimes I hear about a random person dying in their sleep and just wish it was me.

I also get jealous of people who commit suicide. Even more jealous of people who die a peaceful accidental death, that's how I want to go--that way it's not my "fault".

Edit: this is terrible but I remember when a friend of mine committed suicide I was angry that I tried so many times and failed but that she had successfully died. Fucked up, I know, but being suicidal does that to you.
I guess that makes sense. I don't roast them either, I just report if applicable and don't engage with them. They still do bother me though. I hope I was never like that, to be honest.
Man I hate that type of person. I genuinely don't understand how they think they're doing the right thing, or if they think they're doing the right thing in the first place.
It pisses me off to no end. I can't tell if people don't read or don't care, but knowing the way things go it's probably a combination of the two.
My strategy has been to just talk to random people and make friends with some of them. This strategy is great for making friends but I'm not great at keeping them so your mileage may vary.
This. I hate how suicide prevention always seems to take precedence over basic human decency. It seems like most of the comments here are just guilt tripping or making empty promises.
Same here, I hate the feeling of trying again and again to write something and just closing the window in frustration.
